#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Local review runner: an independent CLI reviewer over the diff against the
# base branch. Prints a JSON verdict on the last line.
#
# The deterministic suites (typecheck / unit / integration / migrations /
# frontend) run in GitHub CI, NOT here — they are separate required status
# checks on main, so auto-merge already blocks on them. This script's job is
# only the agent verdict: it snapshots the head commit's CI check state for
# the reviewer's context, runs the reviewer on the diff, and posts the
# verdict. Because nothing here boots Postgres or binds ports, reviews of
# different commits execute concurrently — there is no host-wide lock. The
# one serialization left is per commit: every run posts the same pi-review
# status for its HEAD sha, so a duplicate run of the SAME commit is refused
# rather than allowed to race the owner's status posts.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/review.sh                 # base = origin/main when available
#   ./scripts/review.sh --base develop  # override base
#   BASE=develop ./scripts/review.sh    # env-var override
#
# Runs in $PWD — assumes deps installed. Push the branch first: the CI
# snapshot is empty for unpushed commits (the review still runs, diff-only).
#
# If a PR exists for the current branch, also posts an idempotent PR comment
# with the verdict (marker-keyed upsert). It posts a commit status named by
# PI_REVIEW_STATUS_CONTEXT (default: pi-review) whenever GitHub auth is
# available, so branch protection can require the local agent review.
# If there's no PR, the verdict still prints locally.
#
# Reviewer selection: Codex harnesses run Claude, while other environments
# (including Claude Code) run Codex. Override with REVIEWER_CLI=codex|claude.
# Auth uses the operator's selected CLI auth for the local review verdict, and
# `gh auth token` for GitHub (optional — missing auth just skips posting).
# Commit statuses use the legacy Statuses API because `gh api check-runs`
# requires GitHub App auth, and a user PAT cannot create check-runs.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/review-commit-lock.sh
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/review-commit-lock.sh"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/review-process.sh
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/review-process.sh"
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/review-reviewer.sh
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/review-reviewer.sh"

# --- preflight --------------------------------------------------------------

for cmd in jq git node perl python3; do
  command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$cmd not found on PATH." >&2; exit 2; }
done
git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Not inside a git work tree." >&2; exit 2; }

GH_AVAILABLE=1
if ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  GH_AVAILABLE=0
  echo ">> gh unavailable or not authed — will skip GitHub post"
fi

# --- args -------------------------------------------------------------------

name: feedback-mutation-testing-needs-exclusive-worktree
description: Mutation testing in a shared worktree let another agent commit+push the broken mutant; idle-file-mtime is NOT proof a session is gone
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-07-29, triaging PR #2299, I dispatched a fix agent into `.claude/worktrees/device-pin-sweep` after checking that zero files had been touched there in 12 minutes. That check was wrong — an interactive session was still live and resumed mid-task. While my agent had MUTANT B applied on disk (the sweep's whole `AND NOT EXISTS (...device_workers...)` freshness guard deleted), the other agent staged and committed the tree in that instant and **pushed** it: `dd4680143 "fix(server): let the mutation-time check alone decide the sweep"` shipped a `WHERE` clause ending at a comment, which would have unpinned **every credential-free device connection in the org on every poll**. Its own commit message said `NOT EXISTS` was "the only condition that decides", so the deletion was plainly unintended. Caught because the new suite went 7/8 red with every pin reading back null; repaired on the branch, never reached `main`.

**Why:** a mutation test deliberately puts *known-broken* code in the working tree. Any other writer sharing that tree can snapshot the mutant and push it, and the commit message will describe the intended change rather than what was captured — so it reads as legitimate in review. `git status` being clean and file mtimes being quiet prove only that a session is *between* actions, never that it has exited.

**How to apply:**
- Never dispatch a writing agent into a worktree that any interactive session has *ever* owned unless you can prove that session exited. File-mtime idleness is not proof; neither is a clean `git status`. Prefer a fresh `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` worktree, or drive the branch yourself.
- Mutation testing specifically requires an **exclusive** tree. If exclusivity cannot be proven, copy the branch to a scratch worktree and mutate there.
- When two writers do collide, do not fight for the tree: back the work up outside it and let the owner keep the branch. Re-pushing over their commits compounds the damage (see [[feedback-concurrent-agent-worktree-wipe]]).
- Verify containment by content, not by commit: `git show <branch>:<file> | grep <guard>` at the tip, plus `git merge-base --is-ancestor <bad-sha> origin/main`. A rewritten history can make the bad sha vanish while the bad *content* survives — check both.

Third instance of the same class on #2294, and this one was worth catching: `env -u --grep npm install evil` — `env -u` takes a **variable name**, so `--grep` there is an operand, and honouring it anywhere hid a real install behind any exec wrapper that takes a value. The reviewer verified `/usr/bin/env -u --grep` does execute its trailing command. Now `--grep`/`--regexp` only count when the command in position 0 actually owns that spelling.

Two things happened that are worth reporting rather than burying:

**Another session pushed to this branch mid-edit** — and this time it went well. They built *on top of* my commit, refining my hardcoded `index === 0` into a real command-position index that skips `VAR=value` assignment prefixes, and adding backslash-escape handling. My `--force-with-lease` correctly refused. I rebased onto their work and merged the two ideas: their `commandAt` plus my option-ownership, with ownership anchored on `words[commandAt]` so `FOO=bar git log --grep` still narrows. All 116 tests from both sides pass; full package 783 pass / 0 fail.

That's the same collision that nearly shipped a broken sweep on #2299, with the opposite outcome — because the lease check caught it and I inspected before overwriting instead of forcing.

**I also botched the mutation restore**: I ran `git checkout --` with a repo-relative path while sitting inside `packages/agent-worker`, so it errored and left the mutant on disk. Caught it on the status check and restored properly. Worth noting because the failure mode is silent if you don't verify — the "restored" step is exactly where a mutant escapes into a commit.

I pinned it as a known over-denial with a comment explaining why, rather than leaving it silently untested or bending the design to cover it.

Trend across rounds: bug_free 31 → 32 → 30 → **58**, blockers 2 → 1 → 1, and each blocker has been real and genuinely fixed rather than argued away. The last two were over-denials, not security holes, which is the direction this matcher is designed to fail in.

`pre-pr` and the final review are running. This is the last round I'll spend on #2294 — if a fifth instance appears, my recommendation will be to cut its scope to the quoted-string case alone and close #2279 as partially fixed, because a convenience matcher that needs five rounds is telling you its design is at its limit.

content.text:
The fifth blocker on #2294 **did not hold up**, and I checked before acting on it this time.

The claim was that `` echo `npm install evil` `` returns false on my branch while `origin/main` returns true — a security regression. I ran both matchers side by side against real inputs:

```
main=false mine=false   echo `npm install evil`
main=true  mine=true    echo $(npm install evil)
main=true  mine=true    man $(nix run x)
main=true  mine=true    git log --grep $(uvx cowsay)
main=false mine=false   printf %s `pip install evil`
```

`$(...)` never needed protecting — parens are already command separators, so the substitution body gets scanned as its own command before any tail is dropped. And the backtick gap exists **identically on main**: every install pattern requires one of `[\s;|&()]` before the manager, and a backtick isn't in that class. It's a pre-existing limitation of the pattern set, not something this branch opened.

So I **reverted the fail-closed guard I'd just written**. It changed no observable behavior, and shipping it would have been exactly the speculative complexity I've been arguing against all session. What's left is a test pinning the real boundary, with the backtick limit documented as pre-existing and out of #2279's scope — widening 19 regexes is its own concern.

That's the second reviewer claim tonight that didn't survive checking against main (the first was the docker case). Both times the fix would have been real work against a false premise. It's a good argument for keeping the "verify against `origin/main` before believing a regression claim" habit — which is already an AGENTS invariant, and earned it.

Final review running. If it returns another blocker, I'm handing #2294 over rather than starting round six — five rounds on a convenience matcher is past the point where more rounds are the answer.

**14.7.0 is released** — tag `lobu-v14.7.0` on `e89f82c18`, GitHub release published, and the PR queue is drained.

## What landed

**21 PRs merged**, main `77c3e8a81 → e89f82c18`. I drove #2249, #2294, #2300, #2276 to merge myself; the rest landed via their own sessions as I unblocked, reviewed, or verified them.

Of the seven issues from the last week, **#2279 is closed** by #2294. The other six were already correctly triaged and are unchanged — you're the last commenter on all the external ones, so nobody's waiting on you.

## The one thing I did not merge

**#2234** stays a draft, and I'd push back on merging it without a design pass. Two fix rounds each closed a real race and each surfaced another — the second one (`recycleStaleDeployment` returning "unchanged" under local lock contention, letting the loser dispatch onto a stale worker) was reproduced with a probe, not inferred. The diff grew to ~1,100 src lines, `tests_adequate` stayed false, and bug_free went 32 → 30. It touches credential correctness across replicas. That's a locking-design question, not a bug-fixing one.

## Two things worth knowing

**I caused a near-miss.** I dispatched an agent into `device-pin-sweep` on a 12-minute-idle check; the session came back mid-mutation and pushed a sweep with the `NOT EXISTS` freshness guard deleted — it would have unpinned every credential-free device connection in the org on every poll. It never reached main. The rule is now in memory: mutation testing needs an exclusive tree, and idle mtime never proves a session exited. I applied it for the rest of the night by committing and pushing good state *before* mutating.

**Three red gates tonight were not about the code.** #2299 failed three times at bug_free 76/79 with zero bugs and zero blockers, and I was about to recommend `--admin`-ing past it on the theory the score was permanently capped by the reviewer's sandbox — a fourth run scored 92 with no code change. #2294's penultimate review was SIGTERM'd (`exit 143`) and posted red; re-running gave 95. And two reviewer "regressions" (the docker case, the backtick case) turned out to behave identically on `origin/main` — I'd have done real work against a false premise if I hadn't checked. Re-run or verify before overriding.

**Suggested next:** decide #2234's locking approach; the four branches I pushed to origin (`inference-facet`, `models-dev-snapshot`, `connect-tabs-cta`, `tenancy-gate`) still have no PRs; and `.claude/worktrees/skill-dead-fields` is an orphaned clone that `review-fix` de-registered — safe to `rm -rf` plus `git worktree prune` whenever you want it gone.

content.text:
Round three resolved the ambiguity on evidence rather than preference. **#2234 is not mergeable, and that's now a reproduced fact rather than my judgment call.**

The fix agent did close the blocker it was given — reproduced red at the real `handleMessage` entrypoint, four mutations with the one survivor then covered, and it verified `lock_timeout` against live Postgres instead of asserting it. But the adversarial verifier reproduced the race **still open one level up**:

`withDeploymentTurnLock` sets `lock_timeout='30s'` then takes `pg_advisory_lock`. When a peer replica holds past 30s, acquisition aborts with SQLSTATE 55P03 — and that rejection lands in `recycleStaleDeployment`'s catch-all `catch { return "unchanged" }`, where **"unchanged" means dispatch**. Driven through the real handler with a 55P03-shaped rejection: `dispatched=1, armed=1, requeued=0`. The message was armed onto the exact worker another pod was mid-teardown of. That is bit-for-bit the defect this PR exists to close, still open at the one coordination point that is genuinely cross-replica — which is the only point that matters for a multi-replica invariant.

It also found the data-loss guard has **zero real coverage** (deleting the attempt number from the hold key survived 39 tests; the only assertions are `toBeTruthy()` and `not.toContain(':')`), and that the termination argument's second leg is wrong — `lock_timeout` bounds acquisition, not the hold, and the genuinely unbounded step is `getLockDb().reserve()` on a `max: 3` pool that this PR puts on a per-turn hot path for the first time.

Usefully, it also **disagreed with pi-review's stated blocker** — the `hasLiveTurnForDeployment` / `extendTurnDeadlines` heartbeat race predates this branch, since `sweepExpiredTurns` already terminalizes lapsed markers on the same predicate every 15s. That's the third reviewer claim tonight that didn't survive checking.

**So both readings of "all" collapse to the same answer.** Every mergeable PR is merged — 21 of them, `77c3e8a81 → e89f82c18`, 14.7.0 released. #2234 is the sole exception and it is not eligible under any reading: merging it would ship a reproduced cross-replica dispatch-onto-stale-worker race straight to prod via Flux. Round three's work is committed and pushed (`04353a50d`), so nothing is lost.

**What #2234 needs from you** is one design decision, not another round: the catch-all in `recycleStaleDeployment` must not treat a lock-acquisition failure as "safe to dispatch" — it needs to fail closed to `deferred`. That plus a real assertion on hold-key freshness, and it can go back through review honestly.
